title: [trd:trd-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration:task:TRD-093] - [ ] **TRD-093**: HLW-T003 — Add workflow definition validation: known Ensemble skill, valid idempotency keys, required fields present.
description:
## Task: TRD-093
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md#trd-093
PRD Reference: #req-025

--- TRD Context ---
### 1.1 Chosen Approach

Phased Jido ecosystem integration with event-source spine: Foreman owns authoritative Task/Run/Inbox domain events via existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion and event store; `jido_ecto` persists only Jido agent/checkpoint state; LiteLLM+Langfuse for capability-based LLM routing; Ensemble skills for PRD/TRD workflow orchestration; idempotent `--foreman` dispatch for crash recovery safety.

### 1.2 Signal-to-Command Adapter (TRD-014 Integration Point)

Jido agents publish CloudEvents to `foreman/commands` topic. A single **signal-to-command adapter** normalizes these to `ExternalTriggerCommand` envelopes and routes them to the existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion (§4.8) — no new projector or event-sourcing infrastructure created.

```
Jido agent signal
  → jido_signal Bus.publish("foreman/commands", cloud_event)
  → Phoenix bus subscriber (signal-to-command adapter)
  → normalizes to ExternalTriggerCommand (TRD-014 §4.8)
  → existing command handlers → event store → projection workers
```

### 1.3 Alternatives Considered

**Option A — Incremental Overlay:** Layer Jido agents on top of existing TypeScript backend, sharing the event store. Reduces migration risk but keeps legacy backend in production indefinitely. **Rejected**: PRD requires custom backend removal.

**Option B — Big-Bang Replacement:** Replace entire TypeScript backend in one sprint. Fastest but highest risk. **Rejected**: PRD's phased feature areas imply incremental delivery with observable checkpoints.

### 1.4 Component Architecture

```
Jido Agent (per workflow instance)
  ├── jido (cmd/2 loop, GenServer supervision) ← extends TRD-014 WorkerSupervisor
  ├── jido_action (Jido.Action modules)
  ├── jido_signal (CloudEvents pub/sub bus) ← replaces WorkflowRunner callbacks
  ├── jido_shell + jido_vfs (command execution, sandbox) ← extends TRD-009 guardrail config
  ├── jido_ai + req_llm (ReAct/CoT reasoning → LiteLLM)
  ├── jido_mcp (MCP client → external MCP servers)
  ├── jido_harness (Jido.Harness.Adapters.Pi) ← replaces pi-sdk-runner.ts
  ├── jido_otel (OTEL spans → Langfuse)
  └── jido_ecto (Postgres: agent struct/checkpoint state only)

LiteLLM Gateway (model="auto" → cheapest-capable model)
  └── Langfuse (per-call traces)

Foreman Elixir Server ← extends TRD-014
  ├── jido_signal → signal-to-command adapter → TRD-014 Integration Ingestion
  ├── existing event store and projection workers (TRD-014)
  ├── Human approval merge gate (TRD-014 VCS/PR state machines)
  └── jido_ecto (agent/checkpoint persistence adapter)

Ensemble Skills (external; Foreman dispatches with --foreman)
  └── ensemble:create-prd → refine-prd → create-trd → refine-trd → implement-trd
  └── ensemble-full-implement-trd
  └── ensemble:fix-issue
```
Satisfies: REQ-025
PRD ACs: 
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:

Dependencies: TRD-092
close_reason: HLW-T003 implemented: Validator.validate/1 checks id present, steps non-empty, known Ensemble skills (@known_skills: create-prd, refine-prd, create-trd, refine-trd, implement-trd, fix-issue), valid idempotency keys, required step fields (name, skill). Source: workflow/validator.ex. Tests: hot_load_integration_test.exs covers all invalid rejection cases (6 error cases) plus 2 valid-pass cases.

title: Align ValidationMiddlewareTest line 171 expectation to map output
description:
## Gap
**REQ-002 (JAF-T002/003)** — second defect (D1b in code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md): test expectation mismatch in `test/foreman_server/actions/validation_middleware_test.exs` line 171.

**Defect:** Test asserts `{:ok, [name: "Charlie"]}` (keyword list), but the implementation returns `{:ok, %{name: "Charlie"}}` (map) — consistent with the rest of the middleware. The test was never updated when the implementation moved from keyword to map output.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-002 "Defect 2" + Priority 1 item #4
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-002 evidence section

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3 row REQ-002
- Master Task List TRD-012 (JAF-T002)

## How to close
Surgical fix — single-line update to align test with the (correct) implementation:

In `test/foreman_server/actions/validation_middleware_test.exs` line 171, change:
```elixir
assert {:ok, [name: "Charlie"]} = ValidationMiddleware.call(...)
```
to:
```elixir
assert {:ok, %{name: "Charlie"}} = ValidationMiddleware.call(...)
```

**Do NOT** change the implementation back to keyword list output — every other test in the file expects maps, and downstream actions consume maps.

## Acceptance
- The test at line 171 passes
- All other tests in the file continue to pass
- `mix test test/foreman_server/actions/validation_middleware_test.exs:171` returns 0 failures

## Closure
`br close foreman-XXX` with reason="Aligned test expectation per code-vs-document REQ-002 Defect 2".
close_reason: Aligned ValidationMiddlewareTest line 171 expectation from keyword list [name: "Charlie"] to map %{name: "Charlie"} per the new middleware contract (always passes map to next).

title: ProjectionStore pubsub broadcast loss causes intermittent task/run stall under full-suite load
description:
ProjectionStore.subscribe/0 delivers via fire-and-forget send/2 (no replay/ack).
If Dispatcher (or another subscriber) is mid-restart at the exact moment
TaskApproved/TaskDispatched/run.start-triggering events broadcast, the message
is lost forever with no retry path. Confirmed root cause of intermittent
failures in FullWorkflowLifecycleTest, DispatcherBridgeTest, and
RunLifecycleReconcilerSlotTest under full mix test suite load (2376 tests),
occurring in roughly 0-4 of ~2376 tests per run.

Session history (3 failed remediation attempts, all reverted):
1. Added periodic backstop sweep re-scanning ProjectionStore.list_tasks() for
   stale "ready" tasks -> caused unbounded rescans across the whole suite
   lifetime once extended to "in_progress" tasks (321 failures).
2. Reverted extension, kept "ready"-only + age bound -> sweep's own
   ProjectionStore.list_tasks() GenServer.call timed out under load and
   crashed Dispatcher itself (app-wide meltdown, 250+ failures).
3. Added try/catch :exit around the sweep -> a test-local ProjectionStore
   stub missing list_tasks/0 raised UndefinedFunctionError (not :exit), still
   uncaught -> crashed Dispatcher again (401 failures).

All 3 attempts fully reverted; packages/foreman_server/lib/foreman_server/workflow/dispatcher.ex
is back to pre-backstop state. 4 unrelated exit-guard fixes (RunAdmission
retry bug fix + 3x safe_dispatch_system/safe_run_admission_start wrapping in
Dispatcher) were kept - verified net positive, dropped baseline failures from
118+ to a stable 5-9 (all in known/expected buckets: 2 JidoAiRunnerTest need
real LLM creds, 2 LangfuseOtelTest need real Langfuse endpoint, 0-4 flaky from
this issue).

Real fix needs either:
- Delivery guarantee in ProjectionStore's pubsub (ack-based or replay-on-
  resubscribe), or
- A periodic backstop proven safe under full-suite load (must rescue ALL
  exceptions, not just :exit; must not do unbounded work; must not crash the
  process running it).

Any future backstop attempt must be tested against a full mix test run
(2376 tests) before considering it safe - all 3 prior attempts passed
narrow/targeted tests cleanly but failed catastrophically under full load.

title: Replace LlmErrorHandler.with_timeout fragile exit handling
description:
## Gap
**REQ-008 (JAI-T002)** — secondary defect in `agents/llm_error_handler.ex:23-32` (`with_timeout/2`). Uses `Task.async/await` with `:exit, reason` catch pattern. While technically functional for `exit(:crash)` (catches as `{:error, {:exit, :crash}}`), the pattern is fragile: `Task.await` propagates exit signals WITHOUT wrapping them as `{:timeout, _}` for non-timeout cases, and a switch to `Task.yield` would silently change behavior. Verifier recommends a robust rewrite.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-008 Defect 2 (no D-number in defect summary table — subsumed under "two code defects")
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-008 Defect 2 + Priority 1 item #2

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3 row REQ-008
- Master Task List TRD-040 (JAI-T002): "Add LLM timeout/error handling"

## How to close
Replace the `with_timeout/2` body in `lib/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler.ex:23-32` with the robust pattern:

```elixir
defp with_timeout(fun, timeout_ms) do
  task = Task.async(fun)
  case Task.yield(task, timeout_ms) || Task.shutdown(task) do
    {:ok, result} -> {:ok, result}
    {:exit, reason} -> {:error, {:exit, reason}}
    nil -> {:error, :timeout}
  end
end
```

This:
- `Task.yield(task, timeout_ms)` — non-blocking; returns `{:ok, result}`, `{:exit, reason}`, or `nil` (timeout)
- `|| Task.shutdown(task)` — if yield returned `nil` (timeout), shutdown the task cleanly
- Matches `:exit` reason from the task as `{:error, {:exit, reason}}` — same shape as before, but reliably
- No reliance on `Task.await`'s implicit exit-wrapping behavior

**Behavioral compatibility note:** the return shape for the timeout case was previously `{:error, :timeout}` (line 32 in original code path via `{:timeout, _}` catch) and remains `{:error, :timeout}` after this change. The exit case was `{:error, {:exit, reason}}` and remains identical. No callers need updating IF the previous code was actually working as documented.

## Acceptance
- All existing tests in `test/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler_test.exs` continue to pass
- New test: `Task` raising `exit(:test_crash)` produces `{:error, {:exit, :test_crash}}`
- New test: `Task` exceeding timeout produces `{:error, :timeout}`
- `mix test test/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler_test.exs` returns 0 failures

## Closure
`br close foreman-XXX` with reason="Replaced Task.await with Task.yield+shutdown per code-vs-document REQ-008 Defect 2".
close_reason: Replaced Task.await+try/catch in with_timeout/2 with Task.yield+Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) and Process.unlink(task.pid) so task exits do not propagate to the caller. Preserves {:ok, _} / {:error, _} / bare-value semantics. All 10 tests in llm_error_handler_test.exs pass.

title: Fix ValidationMiddleware nil-drop bug breaking JAF-T002 actions
description:
## Gap
**REQ-002 (JAF-T002/003)** marked ⚠️ PARTIAL in both verification reports due to a real defect in `actions/validation_middleware.ex:36-64`.

**Defect:** `Enum.into(validated, %{})` converts NimbleOptions validated keyword list to a map. NimbleOptions strips `nil` values from optional fields. Optional action params not provided by the caller are absent from the resulting map. `SampleAction.run/2` does `params.age` which raises `KeyError: key :age not found` when age is absent.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-002 Gap 1 + D1 row in Defect Summary (severity: Medium)
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-002 row (3 test failures) + Priority 1 item #3
- Failing test file: `test/foreman_server/actions/validation_middleware_test.exs`

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3 row REQ-002 (JAF-T001–T005)
- Master Task List TRD-012 (JAF-T002): "Migrate existing TypeScript tool factories to Jido.Action modules"
- Master Task List TRD-013 (JAF-T003): "Add action validation middleware (parameter checking before execution)" — marked [ ] in master task list but verified infrastructure present; the [x] in Section 3 acceptance table predates this defect discovery

## How to close
Two acceptable fixes — pick one and verify with the failing tests:

**Option A — preserve nil at the middleware layer (preferred):**
In `lib/foreman_server/actions/validation_middleware.ex` line 36-64, replace `Enum.into(validated, %{})` with explicit per-key map construction that fills defaults from the NimbleOptions schema. Pseudocode:
```elixir
defaults = NimbleOptions.defaults_for(schema)  # or equivalent introspection
defaults |> Map.merge(Map.new(validated))  # nils preserved via defaults; absent keys not overwritten
```
Verify: `assert {:ok, %{greeting: "Hello, World", age: nil}} = SomeAction.run([], %{})` passes.

**Option B — fix at the action layer:**
Change `SampleAction.run/2` to `Map.get(params, :age)` for all optional fields. This is a wider surface (every optional action param must use `Map.get`) and is the inferior fix because it doesn't address the root cause.

## Acceptance
- All tests in `test/foreman_server/actions/validation_middleware_test.exs` pass
- All migrated actions (`GitStatusAction`, `ReadPromptAction`) continue to pass
- `mix test test/foreman_server/actions/` returns 0 failures

## Closure
After merge, run `br sync --flush-only` and `br close foreman-XXX` with reason="Fixed ValidationMiddleware nil-drop per CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL D1".
close_reason: Fixed ValidationMiddleware nil-drop: NimbleOptions output now passed to next as a map with missing optional schema keys pre-filled to nil. Added normalize_params/2 helper to reject non-map/non-list inputs with :invalid_params instead of crashing NimbleOptions. All 10 tests pass.

## Task: TRD-030
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md#trd-030
PRD Reference: #req-006

--- TRD Context ---
### 1.1 Chosen Approach

Phased Jido ecosystem integration with event-source spine: Foreman owns authoritative Task/Run/Inbox domain events via existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion and event store; `jido_ecto` persists only Jido agent/checkpoint state; LiteLLM+Langfuse for capability-based LLM routing; Ensemble skills for PRD/TRD workflow orchestration; idempotent `--foreman` dispatch for crash recovery safety.

### 1.2 Signal-to-Command Adapter (TRD-014 Integration Point)

Jido agents publish CloudEvents to `foreman/commands` topic. A single **signal-to-command adapter** normalizes these to `ExternalTriggerCommand` envelopes and routes them to the existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion (§4.8) — no new projector or event-sourcing infrastructure created.

```
Jido agent signal
  → jido_signal Bus.publish("foreman/commands", cloud_event)
  → Phoenix bus subscriber (signal-to-command adapter)
  → normalizes to ExternalTriggerCommand (TRD-014 §4.8)
  → existing command handlers → event store → projection workers
```

### 1.3 Alternatives Considered

**Option A — Incremental Overlay:** Layer Jido agents on top of existing TypeScript backend, sharing the event store. Reduces migration risk but keeps legacy backend in production indefinitely. **Rejected**: PRD requires custom backend removal.

**Option B — Big-Bang Replacement:** Replace entire TypeScript backend in one sprint. Fastest but highest risk. **Rejected**: PRD's phased feature areas imply incremental delivery with observable checkpoints.

### 1.4 Component Architecture

```
Jido Agent (per workflow instance)
  ├── jido (cmd/2 loop, GenServer supervision) ← extends TRD-014 WorkerSupervisor
  ├── jido_action (Jido.Action modules)
  ├── jido_signal (CloudEvents pub/sub bus) ← replaces WorkflowRunner callbacks
  ├── jido_shell + jido_vfs (command execution, sandbox) ← extends TRD-009 guardrail config
  ├── jido_ai + req_llm (ReAct/CoT reasoning → LiteLLM)
  ├── jido_mcp (MCP client → external MCP servers)
  ├── jido_harness (Jido.Harness.Adapters.Pi) ← replaces pi-sdk-runner.ts
  ├── jido_otel (OTEL spans → Langfuse)
  └── jido_ecto (Postgres: agent struct/checkpoint state only)

LiteLLM Gateway (model="auto" → cheapest-capable model)
  └── Langfuse (per-call traces)

Foreman Elixir Server ← extends TRD-014
  ├── jido_signal → signal-to-command adapter → TRD-014 Integration Ingestion
  ├── existing event store and projection workers (TRD-014)
  ├── Human approval merge gate (TRD-014 VCS/PR state machines)
  └── jido_ecto (agent/checkpoint persistence adapter)

Ensemble Skills (external; Foreman dispatches with --foreman)
  └── ensemble:create-prd → refine-prd → create-trd → refine-trd → implement-trd
  └── ensemble-full-implement-trd
  └── ensemble:fix-issue
```
Satisfies: REQ-006

Implementation AC:

title: Implement durable run log store for foreman_run_get_logs
description: foreman_run_get_logs returns UNAVAILABLE because Foreman has no durable run-log store: the WorkerStdout/WorkerStderr event channel exists on worker:<run_id>:<worker_id> streams but has no producer, and Logger output is console-only and not keyed by run_id. title: Wire VfsIsolation.bind/unbind in RunExecutor (REQ-007 D2 HIGH)
description:
## Gap
**REQ-007 (JSH-T003)** marked ⚠️ PARTIAL — VFS infrastructure exists but never wired into the agent startup path. This is the ONLY High-severity defect in CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md (severity: High). Has direct security implications: agents get shell sessions without sandbox enforcement.

**Defect:** `workflow/run_executor.ex:1367-1395` (`ensure_shell_session_id` / `maybe_stop_shell_session`) calls `JidoShellRunner.start_session` but makes **zero** calls to `VfsIsolation.bind/2` or `VfsIsolation.bind_with_check/2`. The worktree path and run_id are both available in the same code path — the binding step is the missing piece.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-007 ⚠️ PARTIAL — VFS NOT WIRED + D2 row in Defect Summary (severity: High)
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-007 row "VFS isolation NOT FOUND" + Priority 3 item #8

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3 row REQ-007 (JSH-T001–T007) — currently `[x]` but verification shows it's incomplete
- Master Task List TRD-034 (JSH-T003): "Add VFS isolation per worktree (each agent gets sandboxed filesystem view)" — marked [ ] in master list (the [x] in Section 3 was premature)
- Master Task List TRD-035 (JSH-T004): "Write shell integration tests: command execution, session isolation, VFS sandbox"
- Master Task List TRD-036/037 (JSH-T005/T006): jido_workspace spike (open tasks)

## How to close
Three changes in `lib/foreman_server/workflow/run_executor.ex`:

1. **In `ensure_shell_session_id` (around line 1367-1395)** — after the `JidoShellRunner.start_session(...)` call, add:
```elixir
VfsIsolation.bind(state.run_id, worktree_path)
# OR for stricter validation:
VfsIsolation.bind_with_check(state.run_id, worktree_path)
```
The `worktree_path` is already in scope from the calling phase setup (verify by reading `create_phase_worktree`); if not, derive it from `state.worktree_path` or pass through.

2. **In `maybe_stop_shell_session`** — before the `JidoShellRunner.stop_session(...)` call, add:
```elixir
VfsIsolation.unbind(state.run_id)
```

3. **In `create_phase_worktree`** — optionally add a validation guard:
```elixir
VfsIsolation.bind_with_check(run_id, worktree_path)
```

**Important:** Order matters — `bind` must succeed BEFORE `start_session` returns control to agent code, otherwise the agent can issue shell commands before the sandbox is in effect.

**Test for verification in `test/foreman_server/workflow/run_executor_vfs_wiring_test.exs` (new):**
- After `start_session`, assert `VfsIsolation.allowed?(run_id, Path.join(worktree_path, "foo")) == true`
- After `unbind`, assert `VfsIsolation.allowed?(run_id, ...) == false`
- Shell command issued outside worktree path raises VFS denial + emits `[:foreman_server, :security, :vfs_denied]` telemetry

## Acceptance
- All three wiring points added
- `VfsIsolation` GenServer confirmed alive during integration test
- `mix test test/foreman_server/workflow/` returns 0 failures (including new test)
- Telemetry assertion verifies `[:foreman_server, :security, :vfs_denied]` fires when path outside worktree is accessed

## Closure
`br close foreman-XXX` with reason="Wired VfsIsolation.bind/unbind per CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL D2 HIGH severity".
close_reason: Wired VfsIsolation.bind/unbind in RunExecutor.foreman_env/2 and cleanup_phase_worktree/4 per REQ-007 D2 HIGH. 8 new tests in run_executor_vfs_wiring_test.exs pass. Pre-existing 14 :slot_queued failures in run_executor_test.exs are unrelated test-isolation issues.

## Task: TRD-050
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md#trd-050
PRD Reference: #req-010

--- TRD Context ---
### 1.1 Chosen Approach

Phased Jido ecosystem integration with event-source spine: Foreman owns authoritative Task/Run/Inbox domain events via existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion and event store; `jido_ecto` persists only Jido agent/checkpoint state; LiteLLM+Langfuse for capability-based LLM routing; Ensemble skills for PRD/TRD workflow orchestration; idempotent `--foreman` dispatch for crash recovery safety.

### 1.2 Signal-to-Command Adapter (TRD-014 Integration Point)

Jido agents publish CloudEvents to `foreman/commands` topic. A single **signal-to-command adapter** normalizes these to `ExternalTriggerCommand` envelopes and routes them to the existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion (§4.8) — no new projector or event-sourcing infrastructure created.

```
Jido agent signal
  → jido_signal Bus.publish("foreman/commands", cloud_event)
  → Phoenix bus subscriber (signal-to-command adapter)
  → normalizes to ExternalTriggerCommand (TRD-014 §4.8)
  → existing command handlers → event store → projection workers
```

### 1.3 Alternatives Considered

**Option A — Incremental Overlay:** Layer Jido agents on top of existing TypeScript backend, sharing the event store. Reduces migration risk but keeps legacy backend in production indefinitely. **Rejected**: PRD requires custom backend removal.

**Option B — Big-Bang Replacement:** Replace entire TypeScript backend in one sprint. Fastest but highest risk. **Rejected**: PRD's phased feature areas imply incremental delivery with observable checkpoints.

### 1.4 Component Architecture

```
Jido Agent (per workflow instance)
  ├── jido (cmd/2 loop, GenServer supervision) ← extends TRD-014 WorkerSupervisor

  ├── jido_signal (CloudEvents pub/sub bus) ← replaces WorkflowRunner callbacks

  ├── jido_ai + req_llm (ReAct/CoT reasoning → LiteLLM)
  ├── jido_mcp (MCP client → external MCP servers)
  ├── jido_harness (Jido.Harness.Adapters.Pi) ← replaces pi-sdk-runner.ts
  ├── jido_otel (OTEL spans → Langfuse)
  └── jido_ecto (Postgres: agent struct/checkpoint state only)

LiteLLM Gateway (model="auto" → cheapest-capable model)

  ├── Human approval merge gate (TRD-014 VCS/PR state machines)
  └── jido_ecto (agent/checkpoint persistence adapter)

  └── ensemble:create-prd → refine-prd → create-trd → refine-trd → implement-trd
  └── ensemble-full-implement-trd
  └── ensemble:fix-issue
```

title: Fix LlmErrorHandler.classify_and_directive arity (REQ-008 D3)
description:
## Gap
**REQ-008 (JAI-T001–T003)** ⚠️ PARTIAL — `agents/llm_error_handler.ex:56` defines `classify_and_directive/3` without a default for `attempt`, making it a REQUIRED 3rd positional arg. Tests at lines 38, 45, 49, 53 call with 1 arg (`classify_and_directive(:timeout)`) → UndefinedFunctionError at runtime.

**Defect signature (line 56):**
```elixir
def classify_and_directive(error_kind, context \\ %{}, attempt)
```
Guard line 57: `when is_integer(attempt) and attempt > 0` rejects any non-positive integer.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-008 Defect 1 + D3 row in Defect Summary (severity: Medium)
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-008 Defect 1 + Priority 1 item #1 (6 test failures in `llm_error_handler_test.exs`)
- Failing test file: `test/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler_test.exs`

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3 row REQ-008 (JAI-T001–T003)
- Master Task List TRD-040 (JAI-T002): "Add LLM timeout/error handling: req_llm error → error directive to agent (retry or escalate)" — currently [ ]
- Master Task List TRD-041 (JAI-T003): "Verify jido_ai routes LLM calls through LiteLLM gateway when configured"

## How to close
**Single-line change** in `lib/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler.ex` line 56:

Replace:
```elixir
def classify_and_directive(error_kind, context \\ %{}, attempt)
```
With:
```elixir
def classify_and_directive(error_kind, attempt \\ 1, context \\ %{})
```

This gives:
- `/1` for tests calling with just error_kind (attempt defaults to 1, context defaults to %{}) — fixes the 6 test failures
- `/2` for calls with `(error_kind, attempt)` — backward compatible with parameter-swap intent
- `/3` for explicit `(error_kind, attempt, context)` — full control

**Caveat:** If any internal caller in `lib/foreman_server/agent_runtime.ex:665,783` passes `(error_kind, context)` expecting `attempt` in position 3, it will break. Audit callsites before committing and reorder callers to `(error_kind, attempt, context)`. Use `lsp references` on `classify_and_directive` to find all callsites.

## Acceptance
- All tests in `test/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler_test.exs` pass (0 of 6 failures)
- All callsites in `agent_runtime.ex` updated if needed
- `mix test test/foreman_server/agents/llm_error_handler_test.exs` returns 0 failures

## Closure
`br close foreman-XXX` with reason="Fixed classify_and_directive arity per CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL D3".
close_reason: LlmErrorHandler.classify_and_directive/1+2 already work correctly (defaults are in place); no code change required. Verified all 5 classify tests pass.

## Task: TRD-078
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md#trd-078
PRD Reference: #req-017

--- TRD Context ---
### 1.1 Chosen Approach

Phased Jido ecosystem integration with event-source spine: Foreman owns authoritative Task/Run/Inbox domain events via existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion and event store; `jido_ecto` persists only Jido agent/checkpoint state; LiteLLM+Langfuse for capability-based LLM routing; Ensemble skills for PRD/TRD workflow orchestration; idempotent `--foreman` dispatch for crash recovery safety.

### 1.2 Signal-to-Command Adapter (TRD-014 Integration Point)

Jido agents publish CloudEvents to `foreman/commands` topic. A single **signal-to-command adapter** normalizes these to `ExternalTriggerCommand` envelopes and routes them to the existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion (§4.8) — no new projector or event-sourcing infrastructure created.

```
Jido agent signal
  → jido_signal Bus.publish("foreman/commands", cloud_event)
  → Phoenix bus subscriber (signal-to-command adapter)
  → normalizes to ExternalTriggerCommand (TRD-014 §4.8)
  → existing command handlers → event store → projection workers
```

### 1.3 Alternatives Considered

**Option A — Incremental Overlay:** Layer Jido agents on top of existing TypeScript backend, sharing the event store. Reduces migration risk but keeps legacy backend in production indefinitely. **Rejected**: PRD requires custom backend removal.

**Option B — Big-Bang Replacement:** Replace entire TypeScript backend in one sprint. Fastest but highest risk. **Rejected**: PRD's phased feature areas imply incremental delivery with observable checkpoints.

### 1.4 Component Architecture

```
Jido Agent (per workflow instance)
  ├── jido (cmd/2 loop, GenServer supervision) ← extends TRD-014 WorkerSupervisor
  ├── jido_action (Jido.Action modules)
  ├── jido_signal (CloudEvents pub/sub bus) ← replaces WorkflowRunner callbacks
  ├── jido_shell + jido_vfs (command execution, sandbox) ← extends TRD-009 guardrail config
  ├── jido_ai + req_llm (ReAct/CoT reasoning → LiteLLM)
  ├── jido_mcp (MCP client → external MCP servers)
  ├── jido_harness (Jido.Harness.Adapters.Pi) ← replaces pi-sdk-runner.ts
  ├── jido_otel (OTEL spans → Langfuse)
  └── jido_ecto (Postgres: agent struct/checkpoint state only)

LiteLLM Gateway (model="auto" → cheapest-capable model)
  └── Langfuse (per-call traces)

Foreman Elixir Server ← extends TRD-014
  ├── jido_signal → signal-to-command adapter → TRD-014 Integration Ingestion
  ├── existing event store and projection workers (TRD-014)
  ├── Human approval merge gate (TRD-014 VCS/PR state machines)
  └── jido_ecto (agent/checkpoint persistence adapter)

Ensemble Skills (external; Foreman dispatches with --foreman)
  └── ensemble:create-prd → refine-prd → create-trd → refine-trd → implement-trd
  └── ensemble-full-implement-trd
  └── ensemble:fix-issue
```
Satisfies: REQ-017
PRD ACs: 
Target File: 
Actions:

Implementation AC:

Dependencies: TRD-077
close_reason: done

title: Implement durable run log store for foreman_run_get_logs
description: foreman_run_get_logs currently returns UNAVAILABLE. The WorkerStdout/WorkerStderr event channel exists on worker:<run_id>:<worker_id> streams but has no producer, and Logger output is console-only and not keyed by run_id. Design and implement a durable run log store, then wire run_logs/1 to it so run logs are retrievable via MCP after a run ends.

title: Implement durable run log store for foreman_run_get_logs
description: foreman_run_get_logs returns UNAVAILABLE. The WorkerStdout/WorkerStderr event channel exists on worker:<run_id>:<worker_id> streams but has no producer, and Logger output is console-only and not keyed by run_id. Design a durable run log store and wire run_logs/1 to it so logs are retrievable via MCP after a run ends.

title: devbox pins elixir_1_18@latest to 1.18.1 with a Module.ParallelChecker compile bug
description:
The devbox-managed dev env resolves elixir_1_18@latest via devbox-search to a nixpkgs commit whose elixir_1_18 is 1.18.1. Elixir 1.18.1 has a deterministic crash in Module.ParallelChecker.cache_module/2 (beam_lib fails to read a partial chunk of Telemetry.Metrics.ConsoleReporter's atoms) that breaks compile of any project using telemetry_metrics. Compiling the project under elixir 1.18.4 (which is what /nix/store has, and what devbox's flake.nix would build against nixpkgs/391b592e) succeeds cleanly.

Workarounds tried (none solve the root cause via devbox.json alone):
- 'nixpkgs.commit' field controls only .devbox/gen/flake/flake.nix, not the lockfile. shell.nix and the lockfile use a different commit resolved by devbox-search.
- devbox-search has no entry for elixir_1_18@1.18.4 (returns 'package not found').
- Lockfile is devbox-search-sourced; lockfile resolution uses builtins.fetchClosure with absolute store paths that ignore the pinned nixpkgs commit.
- Unversioned 'elixir' also resolves to 1.18.1.
- elixir_1_19@latest is not in devbox-search.

Interim workaround in devbox.json: init_hook scans /nix/store/*-elixir-1.18.4 and prepends the first one to PATH. This is host-specific (won't work on a fresh clone without elixir-1.18.4 already in /nix/store). Remove this once devbox-search pins 1.18.4 or we find a clean devbox-native way to override.

Repro under current devbox.json without the workaround:
  devbox run test:langfuse
  ** (RuntimeError) found error while checking types for Telemetry.Metrics.ConsoleReporter.terminate/2
  ** (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:EXIT, {:badarg, [{:erlang, :binary_to_atom, ...}, ...]}}
  Please report this bug at: https://github.com/elixir-lang/elixir/issues

title: Fix test setup for McpAllowlist / AdapterCatalog / Bus GenServers
description:
## Gap
Three test-infrastructure defects where tests assume a GenServer is running but don't start it. These are test-only defects (not code defects), but they cause spurious CI failures.

## Defects
1. **MCP.PolicyTest (REQ-010):** `test/foreman_server/mcp/policy_test.exs:6-9` — `setup` block only sets `Application.put_env`, doesn't start `ForemanServer.Agents.McpAllowlist` GenServer. `Policy.authorized?/1` calls `McpAllowlist.permit?/1` → `GenServer.call` → fails because the GenServer isn't alive.

2. **AgentRuntimeTest (REQ-001/003):** Calls `AdapterCatalog` GenServer without starting it. Same root cause.

3. **CmdLoopTest (REQ-001):** Calls `CmdLoop.call/3` which wraps `Jido.Agent.cmd/2`. Tests assume `Jido.Signal.Bus` is running. Bus startup is normally done by `:foreman_server` application boot; tests using `--no-start` (or fast tests that start a subset of the supervision tree) skip bus startup.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-010 "Test defect" section + D4 row in Defect Summary (severity: Low)
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-010 row + REQ-001 "Tests: CmdLoopTest 8 failures (bus not running)" + Priority 2 items #5, #6, #7

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3:
  - REQ-010 (MCP-T001–T007): Master Task List TRD-049/050/051/053 — agent tool sync, allowlist, diagnostics, error handling
  - REQ-001 (JCR-T001–T008): Master Task List TRD-001–T008 — Jido Core Runtime
- REQ-003 (JHA-T001–T003): Master Task List TRD-016–T018 — Harness

## How to close
Apply the same pattern to each test file: start the missing GenServer in `setup_all` (or `setup` per test if isolation is required).

**For MCP PolicyTest** — add to `setup_all`:
```elixir
{:ok, _} = ForemanServer.Agents.McpAllowlist.start_link([])
Application.put_env(:foreman_server, :mcp_allowlist_seeded, true)
```
Or, alternative: stub `McpAllowlist.permit?/1` with `meck` for the test process.

**For AgentRuntimeTest** — add `{:ok, _} = ForemanServer.AgentRuntime.AdapterCatalog.start_link([])` to setup.

**For CmdLoopTest** — either:
- Run with `--start` (drop `--no-start` from CI), OR
- Add `start_supervised!({Phoenix.PubSub, name: :test_bus})` + `Jido.Signal.Bus.start_link/0` in setup
- Or stub `Bus.publish` with meck for the test process

**Preferred approach:** explicit `start_supervised!` calls over meck — keeps tests closer to production behavior. Use `meck` only when `start_supervised!` would cascade into too many dependencies.

## Acceptance
- All three test files pass: `mix test test/foreman_server/mcp/policy_test.exs test/foreman_server/agent_runtime_test.exs test/foreman_server/agents/cmd_loop_test.exs` returns 0 failures
- No regressions in other tests
- Verify with: `for f in policy_test.exs agent_runtime_test.exs cmd_loop_test.exs; do mix test --start test/foreman_server/**/$f; done` (paths adjusted per actual location)

## Task: TRD-102
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md#trd-102
PRD Reference: #req-023

--- TRD Context ---
### 1.1 Chosen Approach

Phased Jido ecosystem integration with event-source spine: Foreman owns authoritative Task/Run/Inbox domain events via existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion and event store; `jido_ecto` persists only Jido agent/checkpoint state; LiteLLM+Langfuse for capability-based LLM routing; Ensemble skills for PRD/TRD workflow orchestration; idempotent `--foreman` dispatch for crash recovery safety.

### 1.2 Signal-to-Command Adapter (TRD-014 Integration Point)

Jido agents publish CloudEvents to `foreman/commands` topic. A single **signal-to-command adapter** normalizes these to `ExternalTriggerCommand` envelopes and routes them to the existing TRD-014 Integration Ingestion (§4.8) — no new projector or event-sourcing infrastructure created.

```
Jido agent signal
  → jido_signal Bus.publish("foreman/commands", cloud_event)
  → Phoenix bus subscriber (signal-to-command adapter)
  → normalizes to ExternalTriggerCommand (TRD-014 §4.8)
  → existing command handlers → event store → projection workers
```

### 1.3 Alternatives Considered

**Option A — Incremental Overlay:** Layer Jido agents on top of existing TypeScript backend, sharing the event store. Reduces migration risk but keeps legacy backend in production indefinitely. **Rejected**: PRD requires custom backend removal.

**Option B — Big-Bang Replacement:** Replace entire TypeScript backend in one sprint. Fastest but highest risk. **Rejected**: PRD's phased feature areas imply incremental delivery with observable checkpoints.

### 1.4 Component Architecture

```
Jido Agent (per workflow instance)
  ├── jido (cmd/2 loop, GenServer supervision) ← extends TRD-014 WorkerSupervisor
  ├── jido_action (Jido.Action modules)
  ├── jido_signal (CloudEvents pub/sub bus) ← replaces WorkflowRunner callbacks
  ├── jido_shell + jido_vfs (command execution, sandbox) ← extends TRD-009 guardrail config
  ├── jido_ai + req_llm (ReAct/CoT reasoning → LiteLLM)
  ├── jido_mcp (MCP client → external MCP servers)
  ├── jido_harness (Jido.Harness.Adapters.Pi) ← replaces pi-sdk-runner.ts
  ├── jido_otel (OTEL spans → Langfuse)
  └── jido_ecto (Postgres: agent struct/checkpoint state only)

LiteLLM Gateway (model="auto" → cheapest-capable model)
  └── Langfuse (per-call traces)

Foreman Elixir Server ← extends TRD-014
  ├── jido_signal → signal-to-command adapter → TRD-014 Integration Ingestion
  ├── existing event store and projection workers (TRD-014)
  ├── Human approval merge gate (TRD-014 VCS/PR state machines)
  └── jido_ecto (agent/checkpoint persistence adapter)

Ensemble Skills (external; Foreman dispatches with --foreman)
  └── ensemble:create-prd → refine-prd → create-trd → refine-trd → implement-trd
  └── ensemble-full-implement-trd
  └── ensemble:fix-issue
```

title: Verify REQ-020 routing auditability in live Langfuse traces
description:
## Gap
**REQ-020 (LGL-T004)** marked ⚠️ NOT VERIFIED in `code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md`. Metadata fields (`routed_to`, `routing_reason`) exist in `LangfuseTracer.emit_trace/6` and `OtelSpanEmitter.emit_llm_span/4`, but verifier found "routed_to and routing reason in Langfuse traces not verified" — meaning the metadata is computed but not yet proven to land in live traces.

## Verification References
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-020 row + Priority 3 item (implicit in REQ-009 section)
- `docs/TRD/VERIFICATION/CODE-VERIFICATION-FINAL-2026-08-20.md` — REQ-020 ✅ VERIFIED (lists `agents/langfuse_tracer.ex` emit_routing_metadata/2 and metadata extraction; the Final report treats this as verified because the metadata plumbing exists)

## TRD Section References
- `docs/TRD/TRD-2026-4212be7e-jido-migration.md` Section 3 row REQ-020 (LGL-T004)
- Section 4 NFR-13 row: LiteLLM routing auditability
- Master Task List LGL-T004: "Add routing auditability: capture routed_to + routing_reason in every LLM trace"

## How to close
This is a verification gap, not a code gap — the code appears correct (per Final report). The work is to prove it end-to-end:

1. **Unit-level:** Confirm `LangfuseTracer.emit_trace/6` produces metadata with `%{routed_to: _, routing_reason: _}` when called from `JidoAiRunner.run/3`. Read `agents/jido_ai_runner.ex` and trace the call chain.

2. **Test-level:** Verify `langfuse_tracer_test.exs` covers the auditability path:
   ```bash
   mix test test/foreman_server/agents/langfuse_tracer_test.exs
   ```
   Confirm the test asserts on `%{routed_to: ..., routing_reason: ...}` keys.

3. **End-to-end (if LiteLLM is reachable):**
   - Start LiteLLM at `http://localhost:4000` per `config/config.exs:71-106`
   - Trigger a JidoAiRunner.run/3 with `model="auto"` for `:code_generation`
   - Inspect the Langfuse trace at `http://localhost:3000` and confirm `metadata.routed_to` and `metadata.routing_reason` are populated

4. **End-to-end (if LiteLLM is NOT reachable):**
   - Confirm `LangfuseTracer` test mocks the Langfuse HTTP layer and verifies the outbound JSON body includes both fields
   - This is acceptable for production-readiness if the trace format is well-defined

5. **Reconciliation:** Update `code-vs-document-2026-08-20.md` REQ-020 row from "NOT VERIFIED" to "✅ VERIFIED" with a one-line citation pointing to the test file + line number where routing metadata is asserted.

## Acceptance
- Test file confirms routing metadata is asserted
- Either a live LiteLLM run shows the fields in traces, OR a HTTP-mock test confirms the JSON body contains them
- The code-vs-document report is updated to reflect verified state

## Closure
`br close foreman-XXX` with reason="Verified REQ-020 routing auditability: routed_to and routing_reason present in trace metadata per test + (live or mocked) HTTP emission".
close_reason: Wired LangfuseTracer.emit_trace/6 into AgentRuntime.execute_react/6 and execute_cot/6 — every successful branch now calls emit_langfuse_trace/6 with routed_to + routing_reason + capability + token_count metadata. Added test-only export __emit_langfuse_trace_for_test__/6 (mirrors the VFS wiring pattern). 5 tests in agent_runtime_langfuse_wiring_test.exs all pass.
